manifest_title: GH Real Estate — Federal, HUD, EPA, and FTC Authoritative Source Cache
scope_note: Official current primary law and selected current compliance guidance for a Kansas private residential landlord. Authority tiers and factual triggers must be honored; presence in this cache does not mean every source applies to every property or event.

documents.title: Fair Housing Act — Title VIII, Civil Rights Act of 1968
documents.applicability_trigger: Directly applies to most residential rentals; statutory exemptions must be analyzed narrowly and do not all extend to advertising or 42 U.S.C. § 1982.
documents.currentness: Official 2024 U.S. Code edition; verify later amendments before reliance.

documents.title: Civil Rights statutes, including 42 U.S.C. §§ 1981 and 1982
documents.citation: 42 U.S.C. chapter 21, subchapter I (2024 U.S. Code edition)
documents.applicability_trigger: 42 U.S.C. § 1982 independently prohibits racial discrimination in property transactions; other included provisions have narrower triggers.
documents.currentness: Official 2024 U.S. Code edition; verify later amendments before reliance.

documents.title: Notification of Withdrawal of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity Guidance Documents
documents.authority_tier: Tier 2 — official Federal Register notice of agency action
documents.applicability_trigger: Always relevant when evaluating whether old HUD fair-housing guidance remains in active use.
documents.currentness: Published Apr. 6, 2026; withdrawal effective Sept. 17, 2025.

documents.title: Enforcement Guidance — Assessing Requests for the Use of an Animal as a Reasonable Accommodation Under the Fair Housing Act
documents.authority_tier: Tier 2 — official agency enforcement policy; expressly nonbinding
documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant to assistance-animal accommodation requests; must be read with 42 U.S.C. § 3604(f)(3)(B), 24 C.F.R. § 100.204, controlling case law, and applicable state/local law.
documents.currentness: Dated May 22, 2026. It describes FHEO enforcement priorities and does not itself alter statutes or regulations.
documents.notes: The HUD CDN blocked automated retrieval; cached from a public mirror of the signed 26-page memorandum. Re-verify against the official HUD URL before legal reliance.
documents.render_note: The public-mirror PDF was normalized with Ghostscript to repair malformed font objects; the original mirror file is retained for provenance. Compare content with the official HUD URL before reliance.

documents.title: Fair Housing Enforcement Policy: Occupancy Cases (Keating Memorandum)
documents.authority_tier: Tier 2 — statutorily preserved HUD enforcement policy; rebuttable, not a hard occupancy limit
documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant when adopting or enforcing occupancy standards; two persons per bedroom is only a starting point, subject to unit size/configuration, ages, local code, and other factors.
documents.currentness: Published under Pub. L. 105-276 § 589. Read as enforcement policy, not as a safe harbor that overrides the Fair Housing Act.

documents.title: Joint Statement of HUD and DOJ: Reasonable Accommodations Under the Fair Housing Act
documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant to disability-related requests to change rules, policies, practices, or services. Do not substitute it for the statute, regulation, or controlling precedent.
documents.currentness: Not identified in HUD's Sept. 17, 2025 withdrawal table; verify status at time of use.

documents.title: Joint Statement of HUD and DOJ: Reasonable Modifications Under the Fair Housing Act
documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant to disability-related structural-change requests and allocation of costs; federally assisted housing may have additional Section 504 duties.
documents.currentness: Not identified in HUD's Sept. 17, 2025 withdrawal table; verify status at time of use.

documents.title: Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home
documents.applicability_trigger: Directly relevant to most leases of pre-1978 housing; provide the current pamphlet before the tenant is obligated under the lease, together with required disclosures.
documents.currentness: 2026 edition reflects dust-lead levels effective Jan. 12, 2026.

documents.title: The Lead-Safe Certified Guide to Renovate Right

documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant before covered renovation, repair, or painting work in pre-1978 housing or child-occupied facilities.

documents.title: Small Entity Compliance Guide to Renovate Right

documents.title: Steps to Lead Safe Renovation, Repair and Painting
documents.authority_tier: Tier 3 — official compliance aid; nonbinding explanation of binding RRP rules
documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant to covered renovation/maintenance work and useful as a field checklist; regulations control if the guide differs.
documents.currentness: Revised May 2026.

documents.title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure Rule Fact Sheet
documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant to sales and leases of most pre-1978 housing; use with 42 U.S.C. § 4852d, 24 C.F.R. part 35 subpart A, and 40 C.F.R. part 745 subpart F.
documents.currentness: Document states January 2025; official EPA URL retained.

documents.title: Lessor's Disclosure of Information on Lead-Based Paint and/or Lead-Based Paint Hazards
documents.authority_tier: Tier 3 — official model form; not itself a substitute for compliance analysis
documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant to most pre-1978 leases. Complete accurately, attach records/reports, provide pamphlet, and retain signed acknowledgments as required.
documents.currentness: Official sample form; verify EPA's current form page at time of transaction.

documents.title: Using Consumer Reports: What Landlords Need to Know
documents.authority_tier: Tier 3 — official agency compliance guidance; nonbinding
documents.applicability_trigger: Directly relevant when a landlord or property manager obtains a tenant-screening report or takes adverse action based wholly or partly on it.
documents.currentness: Official FTC page retrieved July 12, 2026; statutes and regulations control.
documents.render_note: Searchable PDF rendered locally from the official FTC page; the archived HTML is retained for provenance.

documents.title: Fair Credit Reporting Act
documents.applicability_trigger: Directly relevant when obtaining or using tenant-screening consumer reports, taking adverse action, furnishing information, or disposing of report data.
documents.currentness: Official 2024 U.S. Code edition; verify later amendments before reliance.

documents.title: Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (E-SIGN)
documents.applicability_trigger: Relevant to electronic leases and records. Section 7003 excludes certain notices involving default, acceleration, repossession, foreclosure, eviction, or the right to cure under a primary-residence lease.
documents.currentness: Official 2024 U.S. Code edition; verify later amendments before reliance.

documents.title: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act
documents.applicability_trigger: Conditional: eviction protection, lease termination, default-judgment affidavits, and related duties trigger with qualifying military service/dependents. Dollar caps are adjusted periodically.
documents.currentness: Official 2024 U.S. Code edition; confirm the current annual rent cap and later amendments.

documents.title: Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act codification, including 15 U.S.C. § 9058
documents.applicability_trigger: Conditional: 15 U.S.C. § 9058(c) notice-to-vacate provision applies only to a covered dwelling in a covered property; coverage depends on federal program or federally backed mortgage facts.
documents.currentness: Official 2024 U.S. Code edition. The chapter is included because GovInfo does not publish the requested section as a standalone PDF.

documents.title: Emergency Economic Stabilization Act codification and Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act note
documents.citation: 12 U.S.C. chapter 52, including note to § 5220 (2024 U.S. Code edition)
documents.applicability_trigger: Conditional: successor-in-interest obligations arise after foreclosure of federally related mortgage loans or on residential real property, subject to bona fide tenancy and purchaser-occupancy provisions.
documents.currentness: Official 2024 U.S. Code edition; the PTFA text appears in the statutory note to 12 U.S.C. § 5220.
